name: Annika Sörenstam
milestone_by_age_26: Won her first LPGA tournament at the 1995 U.S. Women's Open and was named LPGA Player of the Year at age 24.
early_history_summary: Sörenstam began playing golf at age 12 in Bro, Sweden, and joined the Swedish national team at 16. She attended the University of Arizona, winning the NCAA individual championship in 1991, and turned professional in 1992 after winning the world amateur championship.
family_context_summary: Father Tom was an IBM executive and mother Gunilla worked in a bank; the family was middle-class in Bro near Stockholm. Her younger sister Charlotta also became a professional golfer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented that parents had golf-specific expertise, though the family actively played golf together and joined a local golf club.
primary_early_advantage_tags: swedish national team,university of arizona,NCAA champion,golf family
evidence_summary: Sörenstam grew up in a middle-class Swedish family where golf became a shared family activity from age 12. She benefited from Sweden's developing golf infrastructure, the national team pipeline, and NCAA college golf at Arizona. Her first LPGA win at the 1995 U.S. Women's Open at age 24 established her as a dominant force. She would go on to win 72 LPGA tournaments and 10 majors, becoming one of the greatest female golfers in history.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Bro near Stockholm, Sweden; father was an IBM executive and mother worked in a bank.
current_position: Retired from competitive golf in 2008; runs the Annika Academy in Orlando, Florida; widely regarded as one of the greatest female golfers in history with 72 LPGA wins and 10 majors.

trajectory.event: Won NCAA individual championship at the University of Arizona.

Retired from competitive golf with 72 LPGA victories and 10 major championships.

name: Abdul Fatah Younis
milestone_by_age_26: Was a key figure in the 1969 Libyan revolution that brought Muammar Gaddafi to power, personally taking control of Benghazi's radio station at age 25.
early_history_summary: Younis was born in the Jebel Akhdar region of eastern Libya and belonged to the powerful Obeidat tribe. He befriended Gaddafi during army college in the 1960s and joined the military, rising to participate in the 1969 coup that overthrew King Idris.
family_context_summary: Born into the Obeidat tribe of the Banu Sulaym in Cyrenaica, one of the most respected and powerful tribes in Libya. Specific family financial details not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: obeidat tribe,gaddafi inner circle,military academy,1969 revolution
evidence_summary: Younis belonged to one of Libya's most powerful tribes and built a close friendship with Gaddafi during military college. This network positioned him as a key figure in the 1969 revolution at age 25, after which he led Libya's special forces for over four decades. His tribal affiliation and military connections were the primary early advantages documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in 1944 in the Jebel Akhdar region of eastern Libya; member of the Obeidat tribe, one of the most respected and powerful tribes in Libya.
current_position: Died on July 28, 2011 in Benghazi at age 67; final role was chief of staff of Libyan rebel military forces after defecting from Gaddafi's government.

trajectory.event: Enlisted in the Libyan military, beginning his army career.

name: Greg
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first comic series 'Les Aventures de Nestor et Boniface' at age 16 and was working professionally for multiple Franco-Belgian comics magazines by his mid-twenties.

He joined Héroic Albums, then moved to Spirou magazine in 1954 where he worked alongside Franquin, and launched his own magazine Paddy in 1955.

evidence_summary: Greg grew up in Belgium, the epicenter of Franco-Belgian comics, and began publishing professionally at age 16. He benefited from proximity to the Spirou magazine ecosystem and mentorship from André Franquin. By his mid-twenties he was an established comic artist and writer with multiple series, eventually becoming editor-in-chief of Tintin magazine and creating the classic series Achille Talon.
starting_point: Born in 1931 in Ixelles, Belgium; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on October 29, 1999 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, France at age 68; final role was as one of the most prolific French-Belgian comic creators with over 250 comics as writer or illustrator.

name: Miroslav Cerar
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal on the pommel horse at the 1958 World Championships at age 18, and went on to win World Championship gold in 1962 and Olympic gold in 1964, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Cerar was born in Ljubljana and began gymnastics at age 9 after a teacher suggested it to improve his strength. He became Yugoslavia's junior national all-around champion at 16 in 1956, won his first senior national title at 17, and earned his first international medal at the 1958 World Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Ljubljana to parents Pavla and Ivan; father was a naval officer during WWII who spent four years at the Dachau concentration camp, during which time Cerar lived with his maternal grandparents in Turjak.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented that parents had gymnastics or sports-specific expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early gymnastics start,junior national champion,world championship medal,yugoslav national team
evidence_summary: Cerar started gymnastics at age 9 on a teacher's recommendation and showed exceptional talent, becoming junior national champion at 16 and winning his first World Championship medal at 18. His father's wartime absence meant he was raised by grandparents, but there is no evidence of family domain advantage or financial support. His success was driven by early specialization, intense practice, and the Yugoslav national gymnastics pipeline.
starting_point: Born in 1939 in Ljubljana, Yugoslavia; father was a naval officer imprisoned at Dachau during WWII, and Cerar lived with his maternal grandparents during that time.
current_position: Retired gymnast and lawyer; co-founder of the Olympic Committee of Slovenia; inducted into the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 1999; resides in Slovenia.

name: David Irving
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first book 'The Destruction of Dresden' in 1963 at age 25, which became an international bestseller and established his reputation as a researcher.
early_history_summary: Born in Hutton, Essex, Irving was the son of a Royal Navy commander and an illustrator/writer. He attended Brentwood School, studied at Imperial College and UCL, and worked as a steelworker in Germany before writing articles about his experiences. He researched and wrote his first book while working as a night watchman.
family_context_summary: Father was a Royal Navy commander who wrote naval history books; mother was an illustrator and writer. Parents separated when Irving was young, and he was raised by his mother in Essex.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father wrote several books including a history of the Battle of Coronel and the Falkland Isles and a handbook of Naval slang; mother was a professional writer and illustrator.
primary_early_advantage_tags: navy father author,german language skills,archival research,wwii history wave
evidence_summary: Irving grew up in a literary household with a father who wrote naval history books and a mother who was a professional illustrator. He leveraged his German language skills and time working in Germany to access archival sources for his first book on the bombing of Dresden. The book became a bestseller in 1963 at age 25, riding a wave of public interest in WWII bombing morality. His later career was marred by Holocaust denial and legal defeat.
starting_point: Born in 1938 in Hutton, Essex; father was a Royal Navy commander and author of naval history books, mother was a professional illustrator and writer; parents separated when he was young.
current_position: Controversial author and convicted Holocaust denier; financially ruined by a failed libel case in 2000; continues to self-publish through Focal Point Publications; resides in the United Kingdom.

trajectory.event: Published first book 'The Destruction of Dresden,' which became an international bestseller.
